nodes.title: Rödl's question on Ramsey graphs that are locally trees of triangles

nodes.summary: For every natural number $\ell$ there is a finite graph $G$ with at least $\ell$ vertices such that $G \to_2 K_3$, that is, every colouring of the edges of $G$ with two colours contains a monochromatic triangle, and such that for every set $S$ of exactly $\ell$ vertices of $G$, some tree of triangles on the vertex set of $G$ contains every edge of $G$ with both endpoints in $S$.
nodes.title: Ramsey graphs for the triangle that are locally trees of triangles

nodes.summary: Let $s_r(K_3)$ be the least minimum degree of a graph that is $r$-Ramsey-minimal for the triangle, with $s_r(K_3) = 0$ if there is no such graph, as defined for the conjecture. Then $s_r(K_3) = \Theta(r^2 \log r)$ as the natural number $r$ tends to infinity, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm: there are constants $c, C > 0$ such that $c \, r^2 \log r \le s_r(K_3) \le C \, r^2 \log r$ for all sufficiently large…
nodes.title: Minimum degree of minimal Ramsey graphs for the triangle (Guo–Warnke)

nodes.summary: The statement that $s_r(K_3) = \Theta(r^2 \log r)$ as the natural number $r$ tends to infinity, where $s_r(K_3)$ is the least minimum degree of a graph that is $r$-Ramsey-minimal for the triangle ($0$ if there is none) and $\log$ is the natural logarithm: there are constants $c, C > 0$ such that $c \, r^2 \log r \le s_r(K_3) \le C \, r^2 \log r$ for all sufficiently large $r$.
nodes.title: Minimum-degree conjecture for minimal Ramsey graphs of the triangle

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ has minimum degree $d$ when every vertex of $G$ has at least $d$ neighbours and some vertex of $G$ has exactly $d$ neighbours; in particular $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Minimum degree of a finite graph

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ on a vertex set $V$ is locally a tree of triangles on $\ell$ vertices if for every set $S$ of exactly $\ell$ vertices there is a tree of triangles on $V$ that contains every edge of $G$ with both endpoints in $S$.
nodes.title: Graphs that are locally trees of triangles

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ is $r$-Ramsey-minimal for the triangle when $G$ is $r$-Ramsey for the triangle, no proper spanning subgraph of $G$ (a graph on the same vertices whose edges are edges of $G$, missing at least one of them) is $r$-Ramsey for the triangle, and for every vertex $x$ it is false that every symmetric colouring of the ordered pairs of vertices with $r$ colours admits a…
nodes.title: Ramsey-minimal graphs for the triangle

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, $r$ a natural number and $x$ a vertex. The property holds when every colouring $c$ of the ordered pairs of vertices with $r$ colours that is symmetric ($c(a, b) = c(b, a)$) admits three distinct vertices $u, v, w$, all different from $x$, that form a triangle in $G$ with $c(u, v) = c(v, w) = c(w, u)$.
nodes.title: Ramsey property for the triangle after deleting a vertex

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ is $r$-Ramsey for the triangle when every colouring $c$ of the ordered pairs of vertices with $r$ colours that is symmetric ($c(a, b) = c(b, a)$) admits three distinct vertices $u, v, w$ that form a triangle in $G$ with $c(u, v) = c(v, w) = c(w, u)$.
nodes.title: Ramsey graphs for the triangle

nodes.summary: The trees of triangles on a vertex set $V$ are the graphs on $V$ built recursively as follows. A graph whose edges are exactly the three edges of a triangle on distinct vertices $a, b, c$ is a tree of triangles. If $H_0$ is a tree of triangles, $xy$ is an edge of $H_0$, and $z$ is a vertex different from $x$ and $y$ with no neighbours in $H_0$, then the graph obtained from $H_0$ by joining $z$ to $x$ and to $y$ is…
nodes.title: Trees of triangles

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ arrows the triangle in two colours, written $G \to_2 K_3$, if every colouring of the edges of $G$ with two colours contains a monochromatic triangle: three distinct pairwise adjacent vertices whose three edges all have the same colour.
nodes.title: Graphs that arrow the triangle

nodes.summary: For a natural number $r$, $s_r(K_3)$ is the least natural number $d$ such that, for some $n$, some graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ is $r$-Ramsey-minimal for the triangle and has minimum degree $d$; if no such graph exists, $s_r(K_3) = 0$.
nodes.title: Least minimum degree of Ramsey-minimal graphs for the triangle

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
